question: Is the exact eleven-ambiguous-label AUC vulnerability driven by short-followup eels with no real physical receiver contact, or by eels that have a real receiver history, often witnessed operating later with other fish?

classification.zero_real_receiver: No source event at a physical receiver; synthetic release pseudo-stations ignored.
classification.any_real_receiver: At least one source event at a physical receiver.
classification.later_same_receiver_90d: At least one other fish observed at focal eel's last real physical receiver strictly after focal last receiver event and no later than focal release+90 days.
classification.no_later_same_receiver_90d: Complement among 100 ambiguous, including virtual-only and contact-without-witness.
classification.later_same_receiver_1d: Another tag detected at focal last receiver within one day after its last observation, prior to release+90 days.

frozen_target: Original 575-fish 422 vs 153 source-label within-project-year held-out condition-minus-base AUC gain = +0.033555; only source negative labels among the 100 short-followup group may hypothetically switch to positive. No score retraining.
test: For each observationally defined candidate stratum, EXACT minimum AUC increment with k=11 flips and minimum integer k needed to make added AUC nonpositive, if possible. Repeat for complement. Include original 11-fish worst-case witness group composition.
interpretation_boundary: These are counterfactual worst-case label reassignments within measured contact categories. They are not evidence that a particular fish initiated unseen.

A later other-fish receiver event proves only that this receiver observed that other fish at that later time; not continuous uptime, focal tag operation, focal fish presence, or reliable absence detection.
Zero physical contacts in the cleaned migration table does not prove there was no raw detection elsewhere.
Even if a subgroup needs more than 11 strategic flips, that is not its empirical false-negative count.
Pair-weighted AUC, six projects, source-derived labels and fixed project-held-out scores; not migration success, hazard causality or physiology.
